claims.claim: Added an explicit nondefault Runtime consumption API bound to the existing native invocation; default dispatch and terminal ownership remain unchanged.
Positive consumption requires fresh native authentication of exact admission, candidate, reviewed mandatory coverage, latest checkpoint, original feedback and raw/observer captures.
Consumption checks the original registry-held lease, adapter, invocation frame, thread, callback and available profile; immutable invocation intent blocks reconstruction and another invocation.
Local receipts bind authenticated checkpoint/feedback identities and protected Runtime/invocation identities; acknowledgment requires the same adapter's direct typed confirmation.
Exact receipt replay returns original authenticated bytes without proof execution, another callback or counter increments; collisions and ambiguous effects preserve original records and block retry.

Progress requires authenticated scoped committed descendant history, unchanged mandatory proof semantics, prior local consumption and strict reduction of outstanding obligations; every assessment still denies C2.
Outputs explicitly retain STOP, denied production authority and unestablished Human consent/token budget; resource exhaustion, authorization drift and uncertain session state block consumption.
Terminal files/intents, observed source revocation and competing Runtime effects exclude further local authority; failures latch STOP and interrupted effects retain immutable intent.
REPAIR and REMEDIATION consumption return correction-authority BLOCKED and cannot inherit PRIMARY feedback authority.
Closed bounded codecs restrict outputs to factual identities, counters and fixed guarded statuses, reject inconsistent input, and expose no logs, commands, patches or private paths.

Added focused test definitions using real Git/native proof fixtures and actual lease/boundary integration for positive acknowledgment, replay, holder/source faults, terminal contention, crashes, progress and correction spoofing.

The commit changes only eight authorized paths, preserves existing K_i/F_i canonical validators and callable independent APIs, adds scoped AST and cold-import regressions, and documents separate L3-05/L3-06/G3/G6/L4 obligations.
